issues.legal_issue: A compromise term providing for conveyance of property relates to the suit when the property and the consideration for the conveyance fall within the subject matter and relief of that suit.
material_facts: The suit sought recovery of a debt secured by a simple mortgage over the properties in question.
The compromise provided for conveyance of the mortgaged properties for the amount sought in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The conveyance terms related to the suit because the property to be conveyed was entirely included in the mortgage and the sale price was the amount claimed in the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXIII, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a compromise decree may be passed so far as the compromise relates to the suit. A term relates to the suit where it concerns property included in the mortgage that is the basis of the suit and provides for conveyance in return for the amount claimed. No earlier cases were relied upon.

predicates.compromise_decree_in_mortgage_suit: The parties settled a suit seeking recovery of a debt secured by a mortgage, and the court incorporated their settlement into a decree.
predicates.conveyed_property_included_in_mortgage: The compromise provided for conveyance of property that was included in the mortgage underlying the suit.
predicates.conveyance_price_is_amount_claimed: The compromise set the conveyance price at the amount claimed in the suit.
predicates.compromise_terms_relate_to_suit: The compromise terms concern the subject matter or relief of the suit.

issues.definition: When a compromise decree in a mortgage suit provides for conveyance of property included in the mortgage or for a price equal to the amount claimed, its terms relate to the suit.

issues.legal_issue: A compromise term providing for sale of mortgaged property in satisfaction of a decree requires actual conveyance and is not satisfied merely by an agreement to convey.
material_facts: The compromise decree stated that the mortgaged properties were sold for the decree amount in full satisfaction and required the judgment debtors to execute a regular sale deed within ten days.
The judgment debtors did not execute the sale deed.
The decree incorporated the compromise, and the decree holders applied in the execution proceedings for an order requiring execution of the deed.
issues.conclusion: The mere agreement to convey did not satisfy the decree; actual execution of the conveyance was the consideration for the compromise, and the decree holders could seek execution of the sale-deed obligation in the execution proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Order XXIII, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure and construing the compromise as a whole, the Court held that the sale provision did not make the decree satisfied merely upon agreement to convey. Although the sale and the related provisions formed an integrated scheme for adjusting the parties' rights, the obligation to convey remained to be performed. No earlier cases were relied upon.

rule.if: compromise_decree_in_mortgage_suit and property_sold_for_decree_satisfaction and deed_execution_required and not deed_executed

predicates.compromise_decree_in_mortgage_suit: The parties settled a suit seeking recovery of a debt secured by a mortgage, and the court incorporated their settlement into a decree.
predicates.property_sold_for_decree_satisfaction: The compromise stated that the mortgaged property was sold in satisfaction of the decree.
predicates.deed_execution_required: The compromise required the judgment debtors to execute a formal conveyance.
predicates.deed_executed: The judgment debtors executed the required conveyance.
predicates.decree_holder_may_seek_deed_execution_in: The decree holder may seek performance of the conveyance obligation in proceedings to enforce the decree.

issues.definition: If a compromise decree in a mortgage suit provides for sale of the property in satisfaction of the decree, requires a formal conveyance, and that conveyance has not been executed, the decree holder may seek its execution in enforcement proceedings.
